items.title: Notice of Proposed Information Collection Requests: Native American Library Services Basic Grants Notice of Funding Opportunity
tags: National Foundation on the Arts and the Humanities
Institute of Museum and Library Services

agencies: National Foundation on the Arts and the Humanities
Institute of Museum and Library Services
data.abstract: The Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS), as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, conducts a pre-clearance consultation program to provide the general public and federal agencies with an opportunity to comment on proposed and/or continuing collections of information in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act. This program helps to ensure that requested data can be provided in the desired format, reporting burden (time and financial resources) is minimized, collection instruments are clearly understood, and the impact of collection requirements on respondents can be properly assessed. The purpose of this notice is to communicate the agency's intent to request renewal of the clearance for IMLS's Native American Library Services Basic Grants (NAB), a discretionary grant program designed to assist Native American tribes in improving library services for their communities. A copy of the proposed information collection request can be obtained by contacting the individual listed below in the ADDRESSES section of this Notice.

items.title: Perma-Fix Northwest Richland, Inc.; Export License Renewal Application

data.abstract: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is considering approval of an export application, received on August 21, 2026, from Perma-Fix Northwest Richland, Inc. (Perma-Fix). In the application, Perma-Fix seeks to amend and renew existing license, XW027/02, authorizing the export of radioactive waste to Germany. The NRC is providing notice of the opportunity to comment, request a hearing, and petition for leave to intervene on Perma-Fix's application. This action will renew the existing export license for an additional 5 years to expire on September 1, 2031, and amend the existing export license to decrease the total volume of waste from 800,000 kilograms (kg) to 200,000 kg, decrease the maximum activity of all shipments from 8.5 Terabecquerels (TBq) to 2.4 TBq, and add two radionuclides to the license.

items.title: Notice of the In-Person Meeting of the Federal Advisory Committee Known as the Western Water Cooperative Committee

data.abstract: The Western Water Cooperative Committee, a Federal Advisory Committee, provides a forum for discussions between the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers ("Corps") and Western States regarding the operation of Corps projects and water rights and water laws of Western States. The Western Water Cooperative Committee will host an in-person meeting November 17 and 18, 2026, for the Committee to finalize the by-laws and discuss identified opportunities and proposed recommendations to avoid or minimize conflicts between Corps projects and state water rights and water laws. This meeting is open to the public.

items.title: Unleashing the Power of Unlicensed Ultra-Wideband Devices; Petition of Robert Bosch LLC for Amendment of the Part 15 Subpart F Ultra-Wideband Rules; and Petition of Alliance for Automative Innovation et al. To Amend Part 15 of the FCC's Rules To Permit the Operation of Certain Ultra-Wideband Devices

data.abstract: The Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) proposes to update its rules for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) devices to reflect significant technological developments since the rules were first adopted in 2002. UWB technology has matured into a widely used, low-power enabler that supports applications in tracking, automation, precision location, health monitoring, athletic performance, and public safety. As capabilities of UWB have expanded, the existing rules have not kept pace with the technological change, resulting in an increasing number of waiver requests received by the Commission to authorize modern devices. The Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeks comment on revisions intended to modernize the UWB framework, provide greater flexibility for future applications, promote continued innovation, and ensure the protection of incumbent federal and non-federal spectrum users.

Notice of Final Federal Agency Actions on Transportation Project in Nebraska

data.abstract: This notice announces actions taken by the FHWA, on behalf of the Nebraska Department of Transportation and Iowa Department of Transportation, that are final. The action(s) relate to the Decatur Bridge Project, located in Burt County, Nebraska and Monona County, Iowa. Those actions grant licenses, permits, and approvals for the project. The project involves improving the existing Nebraska Highway 51 (N-51)/Iowa Highway 175 (IA-175) crossing of the Missouri River near Decatur, Nebraska. The FHWA's National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) provides details on the Selected Alternative for the proposed improvements.

items.title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Collection; Comment Request

data.abstract: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is announcing an opportunity for the public to comment on CMS' intention to collect information from the public. Under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), federal agencies are required to publish notice in the Federal Register concerning each proposed collection of information (including each proposed extension or reinstatement of an existing collection of information) and to allow 60 days for public comment on the proposed action. Interested persons are invited to send comments regarding our burden estimates or any other aspect of this collection of information, including the necessity and utility of the proposed information collection for the proper performance of the agency's functions, the accuracy of the estimated burden, ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected, and the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology to minimize the information collection burden.

items.title: Notice of Intent To Extend and Continue Concession Contracts and Award a Temporary Concession Contract

data.abstract: The National Park Service (NPS) announces its intent to extend, continue, and award concession contracts in accordance with 36 CFR part 51. To avoid interruptions in visitor services while new long- term contracts are developed and awarded, the NPS intends to extend certain existing contracts, continue others, and issue one temporary contract to maintain essential services until a new competitive contract becomes effective. These administrative actions ensure that visitor services remain uninterrupted across the affected park units.
